chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man drinks a sip from the water and God, Mighty and Majestic, admits him to Paradise by it.

I said: And how is that, O son of the Messenger of God? He said: A man drinks the water, then he stops and puts away the vessel while he still desires it, so he praises God, Mighty and Majestic. Then he returns to it and drinks, then he puts it away while he still desires it, so he praises God, Mighty and Majestic, then he returns and drinks — thus God, Mighty and Majestic, makes Paradise obligatory for him by that.

key_terms.الشربة: a single drink/sip — representing any ordinary act that can be transformed into worship
key_terms.عزّ وجلّ: Mighty and Majestic (Azza wa Jalla) — an honorific formula used when mentioning God
key_terms.فيحمد الله: so he praises God (hamd) — the specific act of gratitude that earns the reward
key_terms.يشتهيه: he desires/craves it — the key element: restraining oneself despite the desire, then praising God

ai.seo_question: How can drinking water become a means of entering Paradise according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that a man can earn Paradise through mindful drinking of water combined with sincere gratitude to God. The practice involves pausing while still thirsty, praising God, and then resuming — this cycle of self-restraint followed by hamd (praise) is what merits the divine reward. This hadith reflects the early Islamic emphasis on transforming even mundane acts like drinking into acts of worship through gratitude and remembrance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that the man drinks the drink from the water, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Enters him into the Paradise by it’.

I said, ‘How is that, O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ The man drinks the water, so he cuts it off, then takes pulls away the container although he desires it, so he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. Then he repeats it, and he drinks, then he pulls it away although he desires it, so he Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, then returns to drinking it. Thus, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Obligates for him due to that, the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:
“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘A man only drinks water but Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, for that reason admits him in paradise.’

I then asked, ‘How can that happen, O child of the Messenger of Allah?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The man drinks water, stops drinking, moves the bowl away when he still has the desire for water, and he praises Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious. He then drinks again, then moves the bowl of water away when he still has the desire for water, then praises Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, then drinks more water and, thus, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, makes paradise necessary for him.’”
